findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed there were two coolers for cold holding foods at 14F or below during the inspection:

(1) The standing refrigerator was observed to malfunction distorting the temperature of various food items stored it. The following food items were discarded due to the refrigerator malfunction.
1. Cheese dips (9 containers) = 49-51F
2. Salsa = 49F
3. carnitas = 52F
4. Tamale =49.2F
5. Sheers cake (2 Containers)= 51F
6. Stuffed peppers = 48.7F
Discussed with PIC that the above items were to be discarded because they had been prepared 3/07/25 and place in the refrigerator from the preparation date. Four containers of beans were observed to have internal temperatures between 39-42F and were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. Ensure that equipments are routinely checked for temperature observation to avoid food spoilage.

(2) The prep cooler at the bar was not cold holding foods above 41F. The following temperatures were reordered:
1. Diced tomatoes 51F
2. Sour scream 55F
3. Guac 55F
The temperature-control for safety (TCS) foods inside the cooler (diced tomatoes, pico, sour cream, cheese, and ranch) were discarded during the inspection. The mango hot sauce was non-TCS and allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC will be using ice baths to keep TCS items inside the cooler below 41F or under. The PIC was instructed to check the temperature regularly to ensure that the ice baths are sufficient for cold holding. The PIC will be using ice baths until the cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.

 The PIC called and scheduled maintenance for tomorrow. The inspector will follow-up to check on the temperatures for both coolers on 3/14/2025. [P]

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Shredded chicken in steam table was at 103F-117F. Cook stated food was heated on stove prior to placing on steam table. Pork & ground beef were at 131F-135F. All 3 pans of food were placed in oven to quickly heat while other foods were being heated on the stove.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment: 750.210a (x2) A) Potentially hazardous foods (PHF) were observed reheating in the steam table - beans were 60F and cheese sauce was 73F-90F. findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and employee did proper steps prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Hands must be washed prior to working with food and all food related items (clean equipment, single service items, etc.), prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and as needed throughout the day when hands become contaminated. Train all employees on proper handwashing/glove use.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 & 151 (x2) - A) Multiple foods in the prep cooler across from the steam table were 48F-60F (shredded cheese, guacamole, pico de gallo, tamales, diced tomatoes, tomato based sauces). Foods at 50F/above were discarded in the trash. Foods at 49F/below were moved to coolers holding at 41F/below. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be held at 41F/below at all times. B) Cooked pork in the walkin cooler had a date of 2/22/12. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods must be used or discarded within 7 days of cooking/prep. Pork was discarded in the trash.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Three pans of refried beans in the walkin cooler prepared on 3/1 at 9:30am were 78F(internal temp - edge of pan)-121F(internal temp - thermal center) at 2:45pm. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hours (total cooling time 6 hours). Beans were discarded during the inspection. **Use ice wand and ice baths to help cool foods quickly. Separate products in to smaller batches no thicker than 4 inches in depth, especially thick foods such as cheese sauce and beans. Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor time and temperature to ensure proper cooling w/in 6 hours.**

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Prep cooler across from stream table was at 50F. Multiple PHF were out of temperature and either discarded or moved to another cooler (see #3a). All refrigeration units used to store PHF shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below. Call for service was made and the repair person arrive during the inspection. Do not use the cooler for permanent cold storage until it is able to maintain products at 41F/below. All products in top portion of prep cooler must be discarded by 6:30 if they are not completely used by that time (4 hour rule for cheese, sour cream, etc.)

Hands are to be washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, between tasks, and as needed when hands become contaminated. Gloves must never be kept on and washed for reuse. Proper handwashing and glove used was discussed with employees and management. Better handwashing/glove use was observed after discussing issues with staff.

Duct tape is not an approved repair material. Remove tape from the freezer and reach-in door handles. Replace the freezer if it can not be easily repaired to be smooth/cleanable. Remove the frozen drink machine if it is not going to be repaired and used.

Sanitizer solution must be maintained at 100ppm chlorine and wet cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. When cloths become soiled place them in the proper soiled linen storage area. Solutions were remade and tested at proper concentration, and the wet cloth was placed in the sanitizer solution.

Food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned and sanitized between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food and other debris. Can opener and knife were taken to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) underside of flat grill and table top fryer (grease buildup); B) black cart; C) cabinets below alcohol counter at bar (dead ants; old mouse droppings); D) prep table in back room; & E) cabinets below order window (food debris). Non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Properly clean the above items and all general surfaces and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - A) Soiled knife was observed on magnetic knife strip with other knives. B) Tubs holding clean utensils and lids were soiled with water and debris. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Do not store soiled knives and other utensils with clean equipment. Keep storage tubs clean to prevent cross contamination of clean equipment/utensils.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Wall behind flat grill and fryers was soiled. Clean the wall and maintain it clean. B) A square opening (appeared to be for an outlet at one time) was observed Inside the cabinet at the bar where mouse droppings were observed. Various cracks and openings were also observed in the cabinet. Provide a proper cover for the square opening in the wall and seal any cracks/gaps in the cabinets.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text: 750.1310 - Spray bottles of insecticide were observed in a cabinet at the bar stored next to boxes of sugar and a bag of plastic holders used for sugar packet storage. All toxic items must be properly stored separate from food and all food related items (i.e. clean equipment, single use articles, etc.) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals. Insecticide bottles were moved to employee restroom for proper storage.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (x2) A) Pan of shredded cheese in ice bath was 60F on top while the bottom was 39F. Cheese was discarded in the trash and fresh product was placed in a new batch of ice. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) in ice baths must be in containers that are adequately surrounded by ice to help maintain products at 41F/below. B) Multiple foods (i.e. sour cream, cheese, salsa) in prep cooler across from steam table were 57F-59F in the middle. PHF in the prep cooler were discarded and non-PHF was kept for use (red sauce, lettuce, and sliced jalapenos). Keep cold PHF at 41F/below at all times.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (x2) A) Small container of cheese sauce sitting out next to the steam table was 94F on top and 109F in the middle. Cheese sauce was discarded. B) Rice sitting out on top of steam table was 117F-125F in the middle. Rice was discarded. Hot foods must be held at 135F/above once they have been cooked to proper temperatures. Do not put containers of food out of steam table wells for any reason. Keep hot foods in the steam table to help maintain proper hot holding temperature. Keep lids on containers between uses/during slow times to also help hold products at 135F/above.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text: 750.210 - Foods in steam table that were to have been heated on the stove first were 127F (refried beans) and 85F on top and 109F-130F in the middle (rice). PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/above throughout the product before being placed in steam tables and other hot holding equipment. Steam tables are meant to hold foods at 135F/above once they have been properly reheated using proper equipment (stove, oven, microwave). Properly reheat food to 165F/above. Use a calibrated, clean/sanitized stem thermometer to check product temperatures. Refried beans were reheated to 200F on the stove; rice was discarded.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Prep cooler across from the steam table was at 60F. All PHF was discarded in the trash (see #3a above). All refrigeration units used to store PHFshall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below. Call for service was made, and the repair person arrived to work on the cooler during the inspection. Do not start using the cooler again for the storage of PHF until it is able to hold products at proper cold holding temperature of 41F/below.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Soft shells were stored out of their original packaging and inside plastic grocery bags. Use clean/sanitized food grade containers for storage of all foods. Do not use plastic grocery bags or garbage bags for storage of any foods. B) Foods on steam table did not have lids on them at the beginning of the inspection, and it was after the lunch rush (~5 customers present). C) Ice bin at wait station was open and drinks were not being made. Keep foods covered during slow periods/between uses to help maintain proper temperature and protect foods from potential contamination. Lids were placed on foods in the steam table and the lids to the ice bin was closed.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - Employee was observed having bare hand contact with soft shells that were not going to be cooked. Employee was observed washing his hands, but gloves or some other barrier (tongs, etc) must be used when handling ready to eat foods. Inspector spoke with manager about handwashing and proper glove use.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.280 - A) Scoops inside salt and other seasonings in the kitchen were down with handles touching foods. Also, scoops had buildup of chunky soil on them. Scoops shall be stored in foods with handles extended up out of the foods. Scoops must also be cleaned/sanitized daily to eliminate buildup of debris and prevent potential cross contamination of products. Scoops were taken to dirty dish area to be cleaned.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text: 750.530 - Employee drink (Gatorade bottle with clear liquid in it) was observed in the prep cooler above/next to foods for customers. Employee drinks shall be stored separate from foods, prep areas, clean dishes, and equipment to avoid potential contamination of foods and food related items. Provide a personal drink storage area, preferably by the handsink, to allow for proper storage of employee drinks. Employees must wash their hands after getting drinks and any other time their hands become contaminated. Employee moved his drink.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) can opener blade (food debris); B) knife by prep cooler (dried food debris); C) scoops in seasonings (dried, chunky debris); & D) drip guard of ice machine (mold). Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and prevent potential cross contamination. Can opener, knife, and scoops were placed in dish area to be clean. Properly clean/sanitize the drip guard of the ice machine as part of routine cleaning schedule.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750.130f & 140b - A) Two buckets of white powder were not labeled. Bulk foods that are not easily identifiable such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the original container shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. The buckets were labeled during the inspection (flour). B) Chicken cooked earlier this morning was cooling in the walkin cooler. the label on the baking sheet had only the date on it. PHF shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Label foods with date and time.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (R) Shredded cheese sitting in a container on top of ice bath in a plastic tub in the kitchen was 70F on top. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at 41F/below throughout the product at all times during storage unless time is being used as a control. The cheese was separated in to two batches and the containers were submerged down in the ice bath. Make sure containers holding PHF that need to be maintained at 41F/below are in ice baths surrounded by ice and not just sitting on top in order to help maintain a temperature of 41F/below throughout the entire product.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - (R) Employee was observed touching shredded cheese with his bare hands when it was being separated out and submerged in the ice bath. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Wear disposable gloves or use some other barrier when handling ready to eat foods. Employee washed his hands and put on a pair of gloves.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Small shelf below soda machine in the bar is worn/rough on the edges. B) Edges of lower shelves at wait station were worn/rough in a few spots. C) Wooden wall mount at the sprayer had peeling paint. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Properly repair the above items so they are smooth and cleanable.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - A Wet wiping cloths were observed on counters throughout the bar, wait station, and kitchen. B) Buckets for sanitizer solution had little to no bleach in them (0-10ppm chlorine). Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microbes. Use test strips to ensure solution is at 100ppm chlorine in order to properly sanitize surfaces. Bleach was added to the buckets during the inspection (100ppm).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Diffuser of Coke nozzle at wait station and can opener in the back room were soiled. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of mold, food, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.850 & 860 - A) Plastic storage bins for utensils by order window were soiled inside. Some of the spoons were stored intermixed w/ handles and food surfaces facing multiple directions. B) Big gray crumbs holding clean utensils had old food debris inside. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other debris. Also store utensils facing one direction with handles extended out. Keep storage bins clean to protect clean utensils from potential contamination.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Wall behind fryers was heavily soiled with grease. B) Wall by door of walkin cooler and attached shelves had dried beef blood splash on them. Walls and attached fixtures must be cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Clean the walls and the shelves in the above areas.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Shredded cheese sitting in a container on top of ice in a plastic tub was 41F in the bottom of the container but was 62F on top. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) shall be maintained at 41F/below throughout the product at all times during storage unless time is being used as a control. The cheese was placed in a smaller container and submerged in ice. Make sure containers holding PHF in ice baths are surrounded by ice and not just sitting on top in order to help maintain a temperature of 41F/below throughout the entire product.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Chicken (2 pans) and refried beans (2 pans) in the walkin cooler were made at noon and were at 75F-138F at 2:30 in the afternoon. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 140F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within 4 hours. Total cooling time is 6 hours. Place foods in shallow pans 2-4 inches in depth in ice baths. Stir foods frequently and monitor the time and temperature to ensure the product is cooling quickly in the proper amount of time. While foods are cooling allow heat to escape by loosely wrapping containers/partially covering pans. Foods in question were discarded in the trash.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Ice bin at bar was uncovered during slow time and drinks were not being made. B) Containers of lettuce and shredded cheese were observed uncovered in the kitchen. C) Sliced limes and cut head of lettuce were uncovered in the prep cooler. D) Black garbage bag was observed being used for bulk flour storage. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Cover ice and other food products between uses to protect them from potential contamination. Store foods in food grade bags/containers. Bag for flour was changed during the inspection, and lid to ice bin was closed.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - Employee was observed touching shredded cheese with bare hands. He appeared to be adjusting the product and not actually making any food for customers. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Use serving utensils or wear gloves when doing anything with ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) soda nozzles/diffusers on both soda machines & B) inside ice machine - lime buildup and dust on drip guard. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of mold and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) prep table holding flour (across from freezers); B) table holding flat grill (grease) ; & C) underside of flat grill (grease/dust). Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces regularly/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text: 750.600 - Sweet/sour bottle at bar was being reused to store mango drink mix. Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items. Any containers purchased with product in them must not be used to store other food products. Once the original product is gone the container must be discarded. Obtain/use food grade containers that are meant to be reused.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - The pipe at the handsink in the bar had a hole in it and appeared to have been repaired with tape at one time. When the handsink was turned on all of the water was coming out of the pipe and getting on the floor. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Have a licensed plumber repair the plumbing at the bar handsink in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor drains and covers at the bar were in general soiled with black buildup. Clean the floor drains and drain covers at the bar. B) Coving was missing at the base of the walls by the kitchen entrance. he junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. Properly seal the floor to wall joint with coving.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Caulk on walls in the dish area and at the handsink in the kitchen was observed to be moldy. Remove the moldy caulk and re-caulk the walls in the dish area and the handsink. B) The walls around the dish machine and below the 3 compartment sink were observed to be in disrepair. Nudo board was pulling away/jagged and gaps were observed around plumbing below the 3 compartment sink. One are of the wall below the 3 compartment sink was soiled with mold buildup. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean and in good repair. Clean and repair the walls in the dish area.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
(CORRECTED) +++In the stand up freezer in the hallway, chicken stored above shrimp and french fries.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Cracked container storing cut up green peppers in the walkin cooler.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
In the front area at the margaritta machine wet blue cloths stored on table top. In the kitchen area on the top of the prep units wet blue towels are stored.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed lights in the back room at small freezer to not have a protective covering.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.
